name: Murias

attributes.attribute: one of the four great cities of the Tuatha De Danann
the home of the Cauldron of Abundance
a sign of plenty that never ran empty

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Murias is a mythological city in Irish tale. It was one of the four great cities of the magical Tuatha De Danann. From Murias came the Cauldron of Abundance. The cauldron traveled to Ireland with the folk of the goddess Danu. It stood as a sign of plenty. In the tales it never ran empty. Food for all who came sat ready within it. Across the Celtic lands the cauldron was a sign of wealth and power. Its use was kept for those of high rank and for festive days. Celtic coinage often showed such a vessel. Murias, then, was one city among the four, each the home of a great treasure.
